conviction_note: This print turns on the first FY2027 guide that includes Megger. The bar for it rests on one estimate source (stockanalysis/S&P, 4 analysts: FY27 EPS $9.22, revenue $1.72B). The revenue consensus looks to under-include Megger, which should make the revenue guide land well above it mechanically. Whether EPS lands above or below the bar depends on how management frames accretion, and my own arithmetic on 6% debt and 5.1M new shares says the effect is close to neutral. Q4 itself sits inside a company guide. The last three events were sold (-2.6, -8.9, -6.8), and an aerospace peer, Woodward, fell on a soft FY27 guide on 2026-11-18. So the findings net to a small positive (+0.7) while p_up stays near 50 (51) on a move I expect to be large (7.5%). The scaled number is therefore about +0.15. The findings sum is larger than the scaled number because the positives are mechanical or rest on a single-source bar, not because they offset.
bar: Q4 FY26: company guide adjusted EPS $2.55-2.65 (Q3 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866706/000110465926092033/tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm). Consensus EPS $2.59 (sweep row), Earnings Whispers $2.65 EPS on $375.4M revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/ESE). FY26 consensus $8.37 implies Q4 about $2.62 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ese/forecast/). The implied Q4 revenue range is $362-392M (FY guide $1.30-1.33B less 9M sales of $938.0M). FY27, which is the line this print most likely trades on: consensus EPS $9.22 and revenue $1.72B from ONE source (stockanalysis.com/S&P Global, 4 analysts). There is no company guide yet, so the FY27 findings are capped small.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 (ended 2026-09-30) is bracketed by the company's own guide: adjusted EPS $2.55-2.65 and implied sales $362-392M. Consensus is $2.59 (sweep), about $2.62 implied by the $8.37 FY consensus, and the whisper is $2.65. ESCO beat Q3 consensus by $0.08 ($2.20 against $2.12), so a print at or slightly above the top of the guide is the base case. The market already expects it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-08-06) beat EPS ($2.20 against $2.12) and raised the FY guide, and the stock went -6.8%. Q2 (2026-05-07) missed on sales and went -8.9%. Beats on the reported quarter have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the result lands inside a guide the company issued, and the whisper sits at the top of that guide. The size is kept small for that reason. If a beat were not priced, consensus would sit at the low end of the guide; it sits mid-to-top.
findings.independence: Consensus and whisper come from different sources (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ese/forecast/, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/ESE). Both anchor on the same company guide.

findings.finding: The FY27 revenue consensus of $1.72B (4 analysts) looks to include only part of Megger. Megger closed 2026-10-01, the first day of FY27, and the company expects about $590M of 2026 revenue from it. Legacy ESCO is guided to $1.30-1.33B for FY26 and grows high single digits. A full-year combined guide would therefore be around $1.95-2.05B, roughly 15% above the consensus average. The company said the FY27 guide will include Megger.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior first-guide event that included a large acquisition is in the baseline. The FY26 initial guide (2025-11-20, EPS $7.50-7.80) drew +2.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap is mechanical acquisition scope, and sophisticated holders will see through it. Headline screens and quant systems that compare guidance with consensus will register it as a large beat. If analysts had fully modelled Megger, the FY27 revenue average would sit near $2.0B, not $1.72B. Sized small because the bar has one source and the market adjusts for scope.
findings.independence: Megger revenue of about $590M comes from the company's 2026-04-15 deal release (https://finviz.com/news/344987/esco-announces-agreement-to-acquire-megger-group-limited). The statement that FY27 guidance will include Megger comes from the 2026-10-01 closing release (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-10-1-esco-completes-acquisition-of-megger-group-limited).

findings.finding: The FY27 EPS bar is $9.22 from one source, which is only about 10% above the FY26 consensus of $8.37, roughly standalone growth. Management said on the Q2 call that Megger is 'accretive to EPS in the first full year' and 'approximately double digit accretive' in year two. If they hold to that, the guide should sit at or above about $9.3. Against that, the deal adds about $0.92B of debt at roughly 6% (CFO, Q3 call) and 5.1M new shares (about 20% dilution). On a deal at about 14x EBITDA that leaves accretion close to zero in year one, so the guide midpoint could land on either side of $9.22.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Megger announcement (2026-04-15) went -2.56% on dilution and leverage concerns. On guidance raises since then, the stock went -6.8% (Aug) despite the raise.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has derated from about $355 to $226 (24.5x the $9.22 FY27 consensus), so a skeptical read on accretion is already in the price. If the market believed the accretion claim, the multiple would not have compressed about 29% in three months with no change in estimates or ratings. Sized small because the bar has one source and the arithmetic cuts both ways.
findings.independence: Debt cost of about 6% and the deal-contingent hedge come from the Q3 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/ESE/Q32026). The $1.5B credit facility and the 5.10M consideration shares come from an 8-K summary (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866706/000110465926113300/tm2626186d1_8k.htm). These are different documents from the accretion claim.

findings.finding: Woodward, an aerospace peer with an October fiscal-year cycle, reported FY26 on 2026-11-18. It guided FY27 sales growth to 6-10% and aerospace growth to 8-13%, a sharp slowdown, with moderating margins. Headlines read 'Woodward falls on soft guidance despite fourth quarter beat'. ESCO's A&D segment, about 50% of sales and led by commercial aerospace and Navy, gives its own FY27 guide the next day, into a sector that has just sold a decelerating guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ESE sold its last two guidance-relevant prints (-8.9%, -6.8%). Woodward's own reaction on 2026-11-18 was negative (size not retrieved).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced already: ESE is -3.8% over 5 days, which may include the peer read. Woodward's slowdown is concentrated in commercial aftermarket (+50% to +24% over three quarters), while ESE's aerospace is mostly OEM content and its Navy and Doble business is a separate driver. Net of the rest of the company (Navy submarines, Doble, Megger), the transmission is small.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview on aftermarket deceleration and the stock-reaction headline (https://finviz.com/news/420898/woodward-closes-a-record-year-as-fading-tailwinds-put-its-fiscal-2027-outlook-on-trial) is a proxy, not a counterparty.

findings.finding: HII reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-29, after ESE last spoke. It booked $32.4B of awards, mainly Virginia-class Block VI and the second Columbia-class build. Newport News revenue rose 18.1% and margin improved to 6.9% from 4.9%, but Ingalls surface-combatant margin fell. This supports the submarine half of ESE's Navy business; ESE already said it is under contract with the primes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Navy commentary has not been isolated as a driver in ESE's past reactions. Maritime surface-ship pushouts were cited in May (that print went -8.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: The awards were public and ESE flagged them on its Q3 call, so this is largely priced. The value is that a direct counterparty confirmed submarine volume ramping after ESE's last update. HII's surface-ship weakness matches ESE's Maritime surface pushouts and limits the upside.
findings.independence: Q3 call: ESE says it is already under contract on Block VI and Columbia (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/ESE/Q32026).

findings.finding: Hubbell reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-27. Utility Solutions organic sales grew about 5%, Grid Infrastructure about 13%, and the 10-Q cites strong transmission, distribution and substation markets. The utility-capex end market for Doble and Megger (now merged into USG) remained healthy after ESE's last update, when Doble orders were up 30%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. The Doble order strength in Q3 did not prevent the -6.8% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer proxy, not a counterparty. The utility-capex story is broadly known, so the finding is small. Hubbell's Grid Automation fell 4%, which marks the limit of the read-through.
findings.independence: ESE Q3 release: Doble orders +30%, condition monitoring +67% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866706/000110465926092033/tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: Management guided NRG (renewables) to another year-over-year decline in Q4 after Q3 sales fell 29%. They expect NRG to return to growth in FY27 off a lower base but not to recover to FY25 levels. NRG margins had fallen to low double digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NRG weakness and utility-segment margin pressure were among the concerns around the -6.8% August reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The weakness is inside what the company already guided, so it is mostly priced. It sits here because the FY27 NRG 'return to growth' claim is tested in this guide.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the Q3 release on NRG -29% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866706/000110465926092033/tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: Boeing's 737 line was 'not stable yet' at 47 a month as of mid-September 2026, with wing production a pinch point. Commercial aerospace OEM build rates, which drive ESE's filtration and fluid-control content, are ramping more slowly than planned.
findings.why_not_priced: Widely reported, so largely priced. A macro proxy with no ESE confirmation; ESE cited an 18,000-aircraft backlog supporting a multi-year ramp.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Woodward's guide (finding 4) is a separate aerospace read.

outside_window.finding: TBG AG received 5.10M ESE consideration shares (about 16% of the new share count), subject to a 12-month transfer restriction. 50% becomes releasable six months after the 2026-10-01 close, around 2027-04-01. That is a supply overhang, but it is dated far after the exit window.

searched_and_found_nothing: A specific cause for the about 29% three-month drawdown into the print (AAII 2026-11-19 and Fox Business pages give none; no rating changes in the month to 2026-11-18). Per the rules this is worth 0.
Any ESE 8-K, preannouncement or Form 4 cluster between the 2026-10-01 Megger close and the print. Searches found none beyond the closing and credit-agreement filings.
A second independent source for the FY27 consensus. Only stockanalysis/S&P was found.
Megger standalone recent trading or margin disclosure. None found beyond the April figures (about $590M revenue, about 14x EBITDA including synergies, $60M synergies over 3 years).
A usable option skew. The chain is unusable per the baseline.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The stock has fallen 36% off its high with sell-side ratings unchanged, which leaves room for a relief rally on a credible accretive guide. The last three events were sold and an aerospace peer was just sold on its FY27 guide, so I hold p_up at 51 rather than leaning long.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar has one source): the FY27 consensus ($9.22, $1.72B) has only one source, so both FY27 guidance findings were cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lessons 5 and 9 (proxy, net of segment): the Woodward read-through applies only to the A&D half and is a peer proxy, so it was cut from -0.7 to -0.5.
Lesson 1 (beats sold): the Q4 reported-quarter finding was already small at +0.3 and p_up is held near 50. Left standing.
Lesson 7: short interest was checked (2.7 days, not crowded) before filing the negatives. Nothing changed.
